chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“A free man is not killed in retaliation for a slave, even if he killed him deliberately; rather, he is made liable for his price, and he is beaten severely if he killed him deliberately.”
And he said: “The diyah of the owned slave is his price.”

key_terms.حُرٌّ: a free person, as opposed to a slave
key_terms.دِيَةُ: blood money or prescribed financial compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a free man deliberately kills a slave in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning retaliation and compensation in the killing of a slave by a free person. It establishes that qiṣāṣ is not applied in this case, while financial liability equal to the slave’s value and a severe beating are imposed, and it clarifies that the diyah of a slave is his price.
